title: autotune: default batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Adds an automated autotune path that sets conservative defaults for batching and KV caching, introduces quantization profiles for common hardware targets, and surfaces unit-economics metrics in the Console and CLI. Backwards-compatible; rollout behind feature flag.
description: Motivation: customers running production workloads repeatedly ask for safer defaults and automated tuning to reduce token unit costs without regressing latency or quality. This PR implements an end-to-end autotune flow that (1) applies conservative batching and KV-cache defaults per model family, (2) ships curated quantization profiles for common GPU types (A100, H100, L4), and (3) exposes per-request unit-economics tooling in Console and the 'redwood' CLI so teams can measure cost impact. Changes are gated behind the runtime.autotune feature flag and rolled out via canary to 10% of requests for 48h before full enablement. What I changed (summary): added a runtime autotuner that suggests and optionally applies batching and cache defaults; added quantization profiles and a profile picker; extended telemetry to emit per-model unit-econ metrics; added a Console dashboard and CLI commands to preview and simulate savings; updated docs and e2e tests. Checklist: [x] Runtime autotune core (suggestions only) implemented; [x] Autosuggest API + config persisted to cluster config store; [x] Quantization profiles added for A100/H100/L4; [x] Unit-econ metrics emitted and wired to Console; [x] CLI: redwood autotune preview / apply / simulate; [x] Integration tests + perf benchmark adjustments; [x] Feature-flag guarded + canary rollout plan. Testing and validation: unit tests added for tuning heuristics and profile selection (runtime/tests/autotune/*). Integration e2e validates a 10k-request replay with and without autotune to verify no >5% regression in P99 latency and >10% median cost reduction in baseline offline workloads. Perf bench was run on internal benchmark-lab; initial perf job showed a transient perf regression on long-context (8k) sequences which was fixed by adjusting the KV-cache warmup heuristic. CI now includes an autotune smoke test and a perf-check stage that runs lightweight replay against cached traces. Backward compatibility and safety: the autotune applies 'suggestions' by default - operators must opt-in to auto-apply suggestions via the cluster setting runtime.autotune.apply=true. When enabled, changes are applied incrementally and instrumented with a rollback policy if error rates or latency exceed configured thresholds. Quantization profiles are additive YAMLs; no existing config is overwritten. Migration docs added at docs/ops/autotune-migration.md. Rollout plan: enable feature flag in canary (10% workload) for 48h, monitor unit-econ and latency SLOs in Console, then gradually increase to 100% with staged deployments across regions. Emergency rollback via feature flag or autoscale group fluidity.
